subject: bare feet
title: What If You Never Wore Shoes Again?

scenes.text: What if you never wore shoes again? Your feet would grow their own, and lose nothing.
Walk barefoot every day, and the skin on your soles thickens into hard calluses.
A 2019 study tested just over 100 adults in Kenya and the US, barefoot walkers and shoe wearers.
The barefoot group had thicker, harder calluses. Yet they felt a poke on the sole just as well.
Thick, cushioned shoes did the opposite. They dulled touch and sent more force up toward your knees.
Calluses don't cushion a step like a shoe. But they guard your skin and still let you feel the ground. Built-in shoes.

description:
What if you never wore shoes again? Habitually barefoot people grow thicker, harder calluses, and a 2019 Nature study found those calluses cost them no sensitivity.
Researchers tested just over 100 adults in Kenya and the United States. Thick calluses protected the skin without dulling touch, while cushioned shoes reduced tactile sensitivity and sent more force up into the joints. People with diabetes or nerve damage should not go barefoot.
